legal_nature.rationale: A second additional protocol to the Budapest Convention, open for signature by States Parties to ETS 185 and subject to ratification, acceptance or approval. It creates binding obligations once in force and is a treaty, not a recommendation.

ratifications.note: Itemised from the Treaty Office chart: Hungary, Serbia, Costa Rica and Japan.

parties.summary: 52 signatories as of 24 November 2026, of which four had ratified (Hungary, Serbia, Costa Rica and Japan). The Protocol is not in force; 48 signatures are not followed by ratification.
unknowns: Because the Protocol is not in force, it has no Parties yet; the four ratifying States are recorded as signatories with a ratification instrument.

relevance.reason: The Second Additional Protocol extends the Budapest Convention's cooperation framework to enhanced cooperation and disclosure of electronic evidence. It is part of the binding cybercrime layer, although it is not yet in force.
